jobs.description:
Company Description

Oakwood is an AI-powered real estate technology startup developing software that helps landlords, property managers, and investors simplify complex operations through automation and intelligent systems. Founded from real-world challenges in Philadelphia's real estate industry, we are building tools that bring fragmented processes into one scalable platform.
We are not simply creating another software product. We are tackling practical problems through AI agents, integrations, reliable engineering, and thoughtful product design. As an early-stage startup, we operate in a competitive, rapidly evolving technology environment. Our ambitions require excellent engineers who combine curiosity, technical discipline, creativity, and a willingness to learn.

Role Description

Oakwood is seeking a Software Engineering & AI Intern who is serious about developing exceptional engineering skills. This is a hands-on, learning-focused opportunity to collaborate with our team, explore modern software systems, and gain exposure to the challenges of building an AI-powered platform from the ground up.
This is an unpaid, six-month internship that requires significant time, consistent participation, and genuine commitment.
It is not a casual or low-effort experience. Startup priorities evolve, technical problems can be difficult, and progress requires focused research, testing, communication, and persistence. We want applicants who understand those realities before applying.
Key Responsibilities

Software Engineering:
Assist with designing, developing, testing, and improving platform features and software components.
AI Development:
Research and experiment with AI agents, large language models, intelligent workflows, and automation.
Backend Systems:
Support learning projects involving APIs, databases, integrations, and data processing.
Technical Research:
Evaluate frameworks, developer tools, and emerging technologies relevant to our product.
Troubleshooting:
Reproduce bugs, investigate root causes, test fixes, and learn sound debugging practices.
Quality and Documentation:
Write tests, document engineering work, and communicate technical findings clearly.
Product Thinking:
Understand user problems, technical trade-offs, and how well-designed software creates value.

Assignments will be aligned with the intern's experience, educational objectives, and the team's capacity to provide mentorship and supervision. Opportunities for greater responsibility will depend on demonstrated skills and appropriate learning goals.

Qualifications

Foundational knowledge of programming, algorithms, data structures, and software development.
Experience with Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or another programming language.
Familiarity with Git, GitHub, APIs, databases, cloud services, or software testing is helpful.
Strong interest in AI systems, machine learning, agentic workflows, or automation.
Ability to research unfamiliar concepts and work through technical challenges thoughtfully.
Personal projects, open-source contributions, or a GitHub portfolio are encouraged.
Clear communication, reliability, collaboration, and openness to constructive feedback.

Students, recent graduates, and self-taught developers with relevant experience are welcome. You do not need expertise in every technology listed. We value demonstrated ability, engineering potential, initiative, and commitment more than credentials alone.

What We Expect

This opportunity calls for substantial effort throughout the full six months. Candidates should be ready to learn continuously, participate in technical discussions, follow through on agreed assignments, document progress, and ask questions when they need support.
We are looking for people who become curious when something breaks, investigate how systems work, and care about building reliable, maintainable software. Strong engineers do more than write code: they consider security, testing, scalability, clarity, and the people who will use their products.

Please do not apply if
you need paid work, cannot realistically participate for six months, want an internship with minimal engagement, or have little interest in software engineering or AI. We respect different financial situations, academic obligations, and career priorities. If this is not the right fit, we encourage you to pursue an opportunity better aligned with your needs.

Compensation & Learning Experience

This internship is unpaid. There is no salary, stipend, or guaranteed financial compensation.
Please evaluate your financial circumstances carefully before applying.
The intended educational experience includes exposure to software architecture, AI workflows, testing, technical documentation, product development, and startup decision-making. Interns may receive mentorship and feedback from team members and opportunities to strengthen their skills through appropriate technical projects. Any portfolio use of project work is subject to confidentiality and intellectual property requirements.

Why You Might Want to Apply

If you love engineering, enjoy exploring AI, and want to understand how a startup develops real technology, Oakwood may offer a valuable learning environment. You can gain firsthand exposure to the engineering process, see how technical ideas are evaluated, and develop stronger judgment through research, experimentation, and collaboration.
We are especially interested in candidates who build personal projects, study unfamiliar technologies, and take initiative because they genuinely enjoy solving problems. We are not expecting perfect engineers. We are looking for people with the foundation, discipline, and ambition to become great ones.

What Oakwood Offers: An Internship That Can Transform Your Career

At Oakwood, we believe the right opportunity, combined with ambition, mentorship, and dedication, can change the direction of someone's career.
This internship is designed to offer more than technical exposure. It is an opportunity to develop as an engineer, gain firsthand experience with emerging AI technologies, collaborate with startup founders and engineers, and understand what it takes to build a technology company from the ground up.
You'll have opportunities to strengthen your technical judgment, develop practical problem-solving skills, explore modern engineering tools, and gain valuable experience in software development and innovation.

What makes this opportunity potentially transformative is the possibility of growth beyond the internship itself.

Six months of focused learning, consistent effort, and professional development can help build the foundation for a stronger engineering career.
As Oakwood expands, exceptional interns may be considered for continued collaboration, additional responsibilities, and potential long-term positions, depending on business needs and available resources.
While future employment is not guaranteed, we want to create an environment where motivated individuals can develop their abilities, discover their potential, build meaningful professional relationships, and potentially grow alongside the company.
For the right person, this could be more than six months of experience. It could be the beginning of a meaningful career in technology.

Six Months as a Bridge to Future Opportunities

We see the six-month period as a potential bridge to a longer professional relationship, not merely a short-term experience. As Oakwood grows, interns who show strong technical progress, reliability, collaboration, and initiative may be considered for an extension, continued collaboration, or potential long-term roles.
Our goal is to identify talented engineers who share our vision and could potentially become important members of Oakwood's engineering organization.
Future positions are not guaranteed.
Any extension or paid employment depends on performance, available openings, company resources, and business needs. The internship does not promise a job, equity, or compensation at its conclusion.

A Message to Serious Applicants

If you have read this description carefully, understand the unpaid six-month commitment
, and genuinely believe this opportunity matches what you are looking for, we invite you to learn more about Oakwood.
Visit our website, research our company, and find our official company email address. If you believe in what we are building, consider reaching out directly.
Introduce yourself, explain why our mission interests you, describe something you have built or a difficult technical problem you solved, and share your resume, GitHub, or portfolio if available.
We appreciate thoughtful, specific messages that demonstrate genuine curiosity, resourcefulness, and initiative. Direct email is optional; applicants who apply through LinkedIn will receive equal consideration.

We are looking for promising engineers who want to learn, contribute thoughtfully, and potentially grow alongside Oakwood as our technology and team evolve.

Important:
This is an unpaid, six-month internship requiring significant dedication. No extension or future employment is guaranteed.

Build front-end architecture and UI components using React and Next.js; create reusable component libraries that support consistent UX across multiple products.
Integrate LLM and AI capabilities into product features using the Anthropic API (Claude) and other model providers; apply prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic workflow patterns to build intelligent, context-aware application experiences.
Translate designs and wireframes into high-quality, accessible, responsive code; leverage AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code) to accelerate implementation without sacrificing quality or security.

Implement responsive, accessible UI designs (WCAG 2.1) that render consistently across devices and browsers.
Write clean, well-tested, and well-documented code; contribute to and enforce engineering standards through trunk-based development and peer code review.

Design and manage relational and NoSQL data models across PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, and MongoDB; optimize queries and data access patterns for performance and cost.
Apply structured prompt engineering techniques—chain-of-thought, few-shot examples, tool use, and system prompt design—to build reliable, production-ready LLM-powered features; evaluate and mitigate prompt injection, hallucination, and data leakage risks.
Partner with UX/UI designers, product managers, and DevOps to deliver features end-to-end; translate program requirements into scalable technical solutions.

Experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL databases (DynamoDB); comfort writing and optimizing queries and managing schema migrations.
Solid understanding of RESTful API design, microservices architecture, and AWS services (API Gateway, Lambda, Cognito, S3, CloudFront).
Proficiency with Git and trunk-based development workflows; experience with GitHub or GitLab for PR-based collaboration.
Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI/CD) and cloud deployment practices on AWS; familiarity with security-focused DevSecOps gates.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to work independently across multiple concurrent projects and communicate technical decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
Comfort working in a regulated, compliance-aware environment; familiarity with NIST 800-171, CMMC, or FedRAMP requirements preferred.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills; proven ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, design, DevOps, and program management teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building AI-powered features using RAG, vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Pinecone), or LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex).
Familiarity with model context protocol (MCP) patterns and structured tool-use design for LLM-integrated applications.

Participate in technical planning, task estimation, and milestone reviews.
Work directly with studio production staff to provide troubleshooting and support during production shoots.

5+ years of professional game development experience with a focus on systems for cinematic content capture, management, and authoring
2+ years of professional experience working in Unreal Engine, ideally with experience working with Unreal Sequencer, animation systems, and audio systems
1+ year professional experience developing desktop applications in C# or similar language
Ability and desire to thrive in a fast-paced production environment

jobs.description:
Background

At Yuzu, we’re building the next-generation health insurance company. We are NOT building a digital brokerage or an AI wrapper - we are going deeper to build the foundational infrastructure required to power tomorrow’s health plans. We believe that software can unlock the ability to build health insurance that is affordable, adaptable, and scalable. Yuzu’s platform will be core to this future.

So how does this actually work? Over 70% of employer-sponsored health plans are self-funded, meaning the employer acts as the insurer and directly covers employees' healthcare costs. This allows companies to customize benefits, gain flexibility, and save money. Self-funded employers partner with a Third-Party Administrator (TPA) to handle the behind-the-scenes plan administration, like processing claims and managing benefits.

The TPA industry is a $500bn sleeper industry that has historically been seen as a services business, bogged down by manual processes and legacy systems (for context, our team couldn’t even access these on our Macs).

Yuzu is a vertically integrated & tech-enabled TPA, currently servicing thousands of employees. We differentiate by helping innovative health plans come to life by facilitating new ways to pay for and access healthcare covered by insurance. Yuzu’s goal is to make it as easy for any business to create and manage a custom health plan as it is to create a storefront on Shopify.

We’re backed by top VC firms and 10+ unicorn founders, including leaders at Stripe, OpenAI, Brex, Deel, Mercury, and Notion, and we’re building a formidable team to tackle the massive opportunity ahead.

Role

Yuzu’s top priority is to ship good software fast. In the last year, engineering headcount quadrupled and our engineering team mitosed into teams . Platform’s mandate is to continue to make it fast, easy, and safe to build Yuzu. If our claims processing volume (or our commits to source control) grow by 100x, we want our systems—and the way we build and operate them—to scale gracefully.

Platform’s customer is the rest of engineering. We are looking for a product-minded engineer who will specialize in platform at Yuzu. You will ship application code, cloud infrastructure, and internal tooling while working closely with the product teams that rely on them. Platform’s mandate is to identify and close gaps in performance, developer experience, and overall quality before they slow Yuzu down.

What We’re Looking For

Finds the Right Path

Different teams often have legitimate but competing needs. You help teams make decisions that hold up as Yuzu grows. Sometimes the right answer is to help one team solve an immediate problem; other times it is to step back and build a shared solution. You can gather input from the right people, make tradeoffs visible, and take responsibility for setting a direction where there is no existing playbook. When you establish a standard, you make it easy to follow without creating friction.

Multiplies Other Engineers

Platform should give other engineering teams more leverage. You care about safe defaults, clear interfaces and documentation, and meaningful observability. You create simple, understandable systems that other engineering teams can extend.

Builds Practical Systems

You start from a real bottleneck, build the smallest useful solution, and use evidence to improve it. You avoid both one-off work and premature abstraction.

Requirements

Curious > Experienced

Many parts of Yuzu are a niche within a niche (e.g., Cash Pay). We don’t expect prior experience in our industry or tech stack, and you do not need to have worked on a platform team before. We do care that you are excited to learn about unfamiliar systems, can identify opportunities for impact, and share what you learn with others.

AI-Native

You use AI to accelerate your own work and are excited to help us discover what high-leverage software engineering looks like today. You care about maintaining consistency and quality as AI increases the pace of change, and you are excited to build CI systems that keep up.

Self-Directed

We are a small team and we don’t have a dedicated PM. You can comfortably find problems on your own, investigate and solve them, and deliver without persistent external direction. You judge when something should be soloed, escalated, collaborated on, or delegated to a more appropriate owner.

Example Projects

Make High-Quality, Prod-Like Data Accessible

How can engineers debug issues in production without accessing PHI? You might work on systems to scrub, synthesize, restore, and develop with that data, finding the right balance of speed and fidelity.

Authentication/Authorization

Yuzu’s is a flexible platform that plan designers use to build highly-customizable health plans. It takes a village to administer a health plan, so how do we make sure everyone gets exactly the right level of permissions? How do you enforce access controls across complex entity relationships, ensure privacy and audit-ability, and let users self-service team permissions, all while guaranteeing excellent performance for checks that are performed on literally every request?

Unify Public API

Each product team owns only a subset of external-facing API endpoints. How do we guarantee a consistent experience for customers and a consistent development experience for engineers?

Brownie Points

You’ve been on-call or otherwise responsible for a significant system in production.
You’ve scaled a system from small to large and lived to tell the tale.
You’ve worked on systems with meaningful reliability, security, privacy, payments, or compliance requirements.
You’ve worked at a large organization with cross-team coordination challenges.
You’ve worked at startup where the engineering team grew far beyond the founders.

Our Commitment to You

You will have significant ownership. Both equity and autonomy.
We will invest in your learning and forgive your mistakes along the way.
We will trust you and tell you everything you want to know about the business.

Compensation

$160k to $240k annual salary, plus a meaningful equity component commensurate with the level of role at a Series A company in NY/SF.

Process

If we interview you, you can expect the following process

Initial 30 minute conversation
A take-home assignment designed to be similar to on-the-job work
A 45 minute fit interview
An onsite super-day
We may speak with 1-2 references you provide

Oakwood is seeking a Software Engineering & AI Intern who is serious about developing exceptional engineering skills. This is a hands-on, learning-focused opportunity to collaborate with our team, explore modern software systems, and gain exposure to the challenges of building an AI-powered platform from the ground up.
This is an unpaid, six-month internship that requires significant time, consistent participation, and genuine commitment.

Software Engineering:

AI Development:
Research and experiment with AI agents, large language models, intelligent workflows, and automation.

Support learning projects involving APIs, databases, integrations, and data processing.
Technical Research:
Evaluate frameworks, developer tools, and emerging technologies relevant to our product.
Troubleshooting:
Reproduce bugs, investigate root causes, test fixes, and learn sound debugging practices.
Quality and Documentation:

Product Thinking:
Understand user problems, technical trade-offs, and how well-designed software creates value.

Foundational knowledge of programming, algorithms, data structures, and software development.
Experience with Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or another programming language.

Strong interest in AI systems, machine learning, agentic workflows, or automation.

Clear communication, reliability, collaboration, and openness to constructive feedback.

new_jobs.description:
Background

At Yuzu, we’re building the next-generation health insurance company. We are NOT building a digital brokerage or an AI wrapper - we are going deeper to build the foundational infrastructure required to power tomorrow’s health plans. We believe that software can unlock the ability to build health insurance that is affordable, adaptable, and scalable. Yuzu’s platform will be core to this future.

So how does this actually work? Over 70% of employer-sponsored health plans are self-funded, meaning the employer acts as the insurer and directly covers employees' healthcare costs. This allows companies to customize benefits, gain flexibility, and save money. Self-funded employers partner with a Third-Party Administrator (TPA) to handle the behind-the-scenes plan administration, like processing claims and managing benefits.

The TPA industry is a $500bn sleeper industry that has historically been seen as a services business, bogged down by manual processes and legacy systems (for context, our team couldn’t even access these on our Macs).

Yuzu is a vertically integrated & tech-enabled TPA, currently servicing thousands of employees. We differentiate by helping innovative health plans come to life by facilitating new ways to pay for and access healthcare covered by insurance. Yuzu’s goal is to make it as easy for any business to create and manage a custom health plan as it is to create a storefront on Shopify.

We’re backed by top VC firms and 10+ unicorn founders, including leaders at Stripe, OpenAI, Brex, Deel, Mercury, and Notion, and we’re building a formidable team to tackle the massive opportunity ahead.

Role

Yuzu’s top priority is to ship good software fast. In the last year, engineering headcount quadrupled and our engineering team mitosed into teams . Platform’s mandate is to continue to make it fast, easy, and safe to build Yuzu. If our claims processing volume (or our commits to source control) grow by 100x, we want our systems—and the way we build and operate them—to scale gracefully.

Platform’s customer is the rest of engineering. We are looking for a product-minded engineer who will specialize in platform at Yuzu. You will ship application code, cloud infrastructure, and internal tooling while working closely with the product teams that rely on them. Platform’s mandate is to identify and close gaps in performance, developer experience, and overall quality before they slow Yuzu down.

What We’re Looking For

Finds the Right Path

Different teams often have legitimate but competing needs. You help teams make decisions that hold up as Yuzu grows. Sometimes the right answer is to help one team solve an immediate problem; other times it is to step back and build a shared solution. You can gather input from the right people, make tradeoffs visible, and take responsibility for setting a direction where there is no existing playbook. When you establish a standard, you make it easy to follow without creating friction.

Multiplies Other Engineers

Platform should give other engineering teams more leverage. You care about safe defaults, clear interfaces and documentation, and meaningful observability. You create simple, understandable systems that other engineering teams can extend.

new_jobs.description:
A high-growth AI-native startup is hiring an ML Engineer in San Francisco to take models from notebook to production and keep them performant, reliable and affordable at scale.

This role sits at the intersection of ML and engineering: strong Python, strong PyTorch, and the engineering maturity to turn models into real product surfaces. You’ll own training, serving, evaluation and the plumbing underneath.

Role: ML Engineer
Salary: $200,000 - $350,000 plus equity
Location: San Francisco, 5 days per week in office

What you’ll be doing:

Train, fine-tune and serve models in production using Python and PyTorch
Build and maintain the inference stack: model serving (vLLM, Triton, custom), batching, caching, cost control
Stand up training infrastructure using Ray, Modal, SageMaker or similar
Work with vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate) for retrieval-heavy workloads
Build evaluation pipelines so model quality is measurable rather than anecdotal
Partner with product and AI engineers to turn research or OSS models into shipped features
Own GPU utilisation, latency and inference cost as first-class concerns
Use AI tooling (Claude, Cursor and similar) across every part of your workflow

What you’ll need:

Strong Python and PyTorch experience with real production ML systems behind you
Experience with Hugging Face Transformers, modern training workflows and distributed training
Hands-on with model serving stacks (vLLM, TensorRT, Triton or equivalent) and GPU-level optimisation
Comfort with experiment tracking (MLflow, Weights & Biases) and reproducibility hygiene
Cloud experience (AWS, GCP or Azure) and modern infra tooling
Fluent in modern AI engineering tools and able to use them to raise output
Happy working 5 days a week in-person with a small, high-intensity team

Nice to have:

Experience fine-tuning or post-training LLMs (SFT, DPO, RLHF)
Low-latency inference work or custom CUDA kernels
Prior work securing or hardening ML systems in production

This role would suit an ML engineer who treats the inference bill, the latency graph and the eval harness as part of their job, not someone else’s.
